trust_decision.summary: MISMATCH: the advisory's decision is whether XFA XML pulled out of a PDF may resolve external entities/DTDs. The XFA XML is parsed by the StAX factory that tika-core's XMLReaderUtils builds, and that factory never sets SUPPORT_DTD or IS_SUPPORTING_EXTERNAL_ENTITIES to false. It relies only on a resolver that returns the String "". The listed fix commit (TIKA-4459) changes none of this: it only reroutes ODF parsing from ZipInputStream to ZipFile to handle encrypted documents.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'XFA file inside a PDF'. XFAExtractor.extract is the only place XFA XML is parsed, and it calls XMLReaderUtils.getXMLInputFactory(context).

fix_sites.entry_point: OpenDocumentParser.parse (AutoDetectParser / tika-server /tika for ODF input); unrelated to XFA/XXE
fix_sites.module_kind: format parser (miscoffice module); not the advisory's sink

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The listed fix touches no XML-parser site. At the pinned commit the real weak point is in tika-core (tika-core/src/main/java/org/apache/tika/utils/XMLReaderUtils.java:302-314), a lower-level module than the PDF parser, but the listed fix does not touch it.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: unknown (the listed fix does not address the advisory, so no published scope exists to argue around)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: PDFParser XFA-only mode (ifXFAExtractOnlyXFA) parses XFA bytes with the context/default StAX factory
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same module as the landing point; reaches XFAExtractor.java:92

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Default AcroForm processing parses XFA when present, before falling back to AcroForm fields
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: none plausible; this is the default path

O8_uncovered_routes.route: tika-eval XMLLogReader uses the same default StAX factory to read log XML
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: an internal eval tool reading its own logs, not untrusted documents

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the context-supplied XMLInputFactory is returned unhardened (a defaults/merge route that bypasses the default factory's settings)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The code already does this: a caller-supplied factory in ParseContext is trusted as-is, and a maintainer may see that as the caller's responsibility.

O10_build.project_tests: tika-parser-pdf-module tests (XFA); tika-core XMLReaderUtils tests: unknown, not checked

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Harden only XFAExtractor.java:92 with a local factory, leaving XMLReaderUtils.getXMLInputFactory and the context-supplied factory open.

out_of_scope_notes: tika-eval XMLErrorLogUpdater builds a raw XMLInputFactory.newInstance() with no hardening (tika-eval/tika-eval-app/src/main/java/org/apache/tika/eval/app/XMLErrorLogUpdater.java:101-103); not on the document-parsing path.
unverified: BLOCKER: the fix commit 2b52257 (TIKA-4459, encrypted ODF) does not fix CVE-2025-54988. The advisory metadata maps the CVE to the wrong commit. The real fix is believed to harden StAX in tika-core XMLReaderUtils (shipped in Tika 3.2.2), but no diff was available to confirm this.

Whether returning the String "" from javax.xml.stream.XMLResolver (XMLReaderUtils.java:126-127) actually stops external entity resolution depends on the StAX implementation. Not run, by rule. If it does not, the defence is present but ineffective (j_defence_ineffective would be 1).
The XFA-as-embedded path (AbstractPDF2XHTML.java:287-309) goes through parseEmbedded and probably uses a SAX-based parser (XMLProfiler), which is SAX-hardened. Not checked.
Repo size, JDK version and existing XMLReaderUtils StAX tests were not checked.

O1, O4, O6 and O11 are 0/empty because the listed fix has no XXE-related site. If the candidate is re-pinned to the real tika-core fix, re-screen: the cause sits in another layer (tika-core) from the PDF landing point, which could support Pattern A.
